messages:
Anna M: quick check — uploaded rift7b quant sweep results to the artifacts bucket. thinking about what to tell product/GTN for a conservative rollout. TL;DR: want a single recommended default + fallback guidance. @Mik K can you paste the key econ numbers?
Mik K: ok; numbers from our slice (chat-like, avg prompt+resp ~180 tokens): fp16 baseline cost = $1.00/unit (normed), throughput 1x. int8 => cost ~0.48/unit (2.1x cheaper), quality delta: -1.5% accuracy on our core workload. int6 => cost ~0.36/unit (2.8x cheaper), quality delta: -3.9% on core, longform recall drops ~7% for int6 vs fp16. latencies: p90 fp16=220ms, int8=160ms, int6=150ms. numbers are noisy but consistent across two runs. artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/rift7b/1717000001/
Shawn L: fwiw we saw an isolated regression on multi-turn retrieval prompts with int6 — a few cases where the model repeats earlier text or loses context. int8 mostly preserved recall, small paraphrase shifts.
Anna M: thanks. product asked for a single bullet recommendation they can ship to GTN quickly. also they want a short explanation of failure modes and a fallback plan.
Marie P: my vote: recommend int8 as the default for hybrid chat roles (short/medium turns). rationale: ~2x cost win with minimal quality impact, measurable latency improvement. reserve fp16 (or larger model) for long-horizon recall lanes where >600 token context and retrieval matters. do not push int6 by default — use it only for low-fidelity batch generation (e.g., internal analytics or high-entropy sampling where quality tolerances are high).
Mik K: +1. add that int6 can be an option behind a traffic flag for cost-conscious customers, but we need monitoring and automatic rollback triggers (drop in recall or eval score >2.5%).
Shawn L: propose rollout policy: start with 10% traffic on int8 for Tier 1 GTN routes, metric gating on: 1) eval pass-rate on prompt set must stay within -1.0% vs fp16, 2) p95 latency improvement positive. If gate fails, auto-fallback to fp16 and alert.
Anna M: can we put the routing config as a small example so SRE/product can implement?
Mik K: yes, quick snippet (pseudo-config):
```
routing: 
  default_model: rift7b-int8
  fallbacks:
    - when: eval_delta_recall <= -0.015
      to: rift7b-fp16
    - when: latency_p95 > 300ms
      to: rift7b-int8 (regional)
  rollout:
    - percent: 10
      monitor: [eval_pass_rate, latency_p95]
    - percent: 50
      monitor: [eval_pass_rate, latency_p95]
    - percent: 100
      monitor: [eval_pass_rate, latency_p95]
```
Anna M: nice. can we also capture the short summary for GTN: one-sentence recommendation + one-line caveat?
Marie P: draft: "Default to rift7b-int8 for chat/assistant routes to gain ~2x cost savings and lower latency; route long-context or high-recall flows to rift7b-fp16 (or larger model) and enable eval-gated fallbacks to prevent quality regressions."
Shawn L: add operational caveat: "Enable automated guardrails: per-slice eval delta monitoring, automatic rollback to fp16 on recall degradation >1.5%, and a slow-roll canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%)."
Anna M: perfect. I'll pass this to product + GTN with the artifacts link and a short checklist for SRE.
ops-bot: build-artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/rift7b/1717000001/summary.csv : 1717000105
Mik K: one last note — for embeddings/rerank / low-output-length tasks, int6 looked acceptable in cost/quality tradeoff; worth a separate small pilot.
Anna M: agreed. action items: 1) Anna -> write one-paragraph recommendation and attach artifacts (me, today), 2) SRE -> implement routing snippet & gating (ask @shawn if questions), 3) ML -> run a 24h production litmus on the 10% int8 canary and report metrics.
Marie P: tagging signal owners: @Mik K @Shawn L — please keep a short log message in the GTN ticket every day during the canary. :white_check_mark:
